note: Submodule of markdownify. Implements hook_markdownify_entity_build_alter to render every file-type field through the md_file_attachment_file_embed formatter during Markdown generation: allowed extension AND within size cap -> inline the file contents (file_get_contents), else filename+URL only. Config object markdownify_file_attachment.settings: allowed_extensions (default [txt,yml,yaml,wsdl,json]), max_file_embed_size (default '1 MB', schema type bytes). Settings form at /admin/config/services/markdownify/file-attachment (perm administer site configuration). Medium/hard cases are grounded in that real config and verified live.

evals.prompt: What does the markdownify_file_attachment submodule do to file fields when Markdownify renders an entity, and which file types does it embed inline by default?
evals.expected_output: It renders file fields through the md_file_attachment_file_embed formatter during Markdown generation, embedding the actual file contents inline for allowed small files (default allowed_extensions: txt, yml, yaml, wsdl, json) within the size cap; other files are shown as a filename + URL link only.

evals.prompt: Which two settings control markdownify_file_attachment, what is the config object, and where is the settings form?
evals.expected_output: Config object markdownify_file_attachment.settings with allowed_extensions (which extensions get inlined) and max_file_embed_size (size cap above which files are only linked). The form is at /admin/config/services/markdownify/file-attachment (permission: administer site configuration).

evals.prompt: What is the machine name of the field formatter that markdownify_file_attachment uses to embed files, and what decides whether a file's contents are inlined vs just linked?
evals.expected_output: The formatter is md_file_attachment_file_embed (MdFileAttachmentFieldFormatter). A file's contents are inlined only when its extension is in allowed_extensions AND its size is <= max_file_embed_size (capped at PHP upload max); otherwise only the filename + absolute URL is shown.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, which file extensions will markdownify_file_attachment embed inline in Markdown? Inspect the live configuration and list them.
evals.expected_output: The allowed_extensions in markdownify_file_attachment.settings are txt, json and log on this site (the 'log' extension is the distinctive one added to the default set).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, what is the maximum file size that markdownify_file_attachment will embed inline (above which a file is only linked)? Inspect the live configuration and give the value.
evals.expected_output: max_file_embed_size is 512 KB in markdownify_file_attachment.settings, so files larger than 512 KB are linked rather than inlined.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure markdownify_file_attachment so that attached .csv files also get their contents embedded inline in Markdown output (keep the existing allowed types too). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Add 'csv' to markdownify_file_attachment.settings:allowed_extensions (keeping txt/yml/yaml/wsdl/json), e.g. via the settings form or a config edit that appends 'csv'.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, raise the markdownify_file_attachment inline-embed size limit so that files up to 2 MB are embedded inline instead of only linked. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set markdownify_file_attachment.settings:max_file_embed_size to 2 MB (e.g. `drush cset ... max_file_embed_size '2 MB'`), i.e. Bytes::toNumber resolves to 2097152.
